judgment.rationale: Both Indicators sit under the same BASIC 4 Content Standard B4.1.1.1 (quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals up to 100,000) in Strand 1 Number, Sub-strand Counting, Representation & Cardinality, and both are at the same resolved coordinate rank (BASIC 4, rank 0). B4.1.1.1.6 addresses skip counting forwards and backwards in 50s and 100s to/from 10000 (LCs: skip count forwards / backwards in 50s and 100s up to 10000), while B4.1.1.1.2 addresses reading and writing numbers in figures and words up to 100,000 (LCs: read / write numbers in figures and words). These are complementary large-number skills — counting sequences versus symbolic and verbal number naming — that mutually reinforce place-value understanding, but the bounded evidence shows no substantive same-rank developmental dependency in either direction (skip counting in 50s/100s does not require written number names to 100,000, nor vice versa), so a symmetric coherence relation is the supported judgment. Both endpoints' source evidence is truncated and carries upstream audit/merge/code context, which limits but does not contradict this reading.

B4.4.1.2.2 extends that same many-to-one correspondence idea to a more demanding application: solving 'how many altogether', comparing, and take-apart problems by interpreting many-to-one bar graphs up to 4 categories (its three LCs are all problem-solving via interpretation), under Content Standard B4.4.1.2 (construct and interpret pictographs and bar graphs to draw conclusions). Fluency in displaying/constructing many-to-one graphs supports success in reading those scales to solve multi-step data problems, so the developmental direction runs second-to-first. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (rank 0, same coordinate) in Strand 2: Algebra, but sit in different sub-strands with different parent Content Standards: B4.2.2.1.1 'Write a given problem as an equation in which a symbol is used to represent an unknown number' (Unknowns, Expressions and Equations) and B4.2.1.3.1 'Translate the information in a given problem into a table or char[t]' (Patterns and Relationships; parent standard represents/describes/extends patterns using charts and tables to solve problems). They share the substantive skill of mathematizing a given word problem into a formal representation — an equation with a symbolic unknown versus a table/chart — so they are complementary representational skills that reinforce one another. Neither statement's text or LC evidence shows the symbolic-equation work presupposing tabular representation or vice versa, and same-rank placement offers no developmental ordering, so a symmetric relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than buildsTowards. Shared tokens ('a', 'given', 'in', 'problem'), adjacent source pages, and the weak 'b4.2' code prefix were treated as nomination signals only. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated and both carry upstream audit/merge context, but the trustworthy statement text and hierarchy suffice for this conceptual-coherence judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are BASIC 4 Indicators (rank 0) in Strand 4: Data, Sub-strand 1 (Data Collection, Organization, Presentation, Interpretation and Analysis), but sit under different Content Standards. The second (B4.4.1.1.4) asks learners to find examples of graphs using many-to-one correspondence in print/electronic media and describe the correspondence used, with LCs 'find examples of graphs in which many-to-one correspondence is used' and 'describe the many-to-one correspondence used in graphs' — recognition and interpretation of an existing key/scale. The first (B4.4.1.2.1) asks learners to identify common features of many-to-one graphs and then construct their own bar graphs or pictographs complete with title, labelled axes and key/legend for up to 4 categories (parent standard B4.4.1.2 'Construct and interpret pictographs and bar graphs involving many-to-one correspondence'). Since ranks are equal, direction rests on this substantive shift from describing the correspondence in given media graphs to applying it in producing correctly keyed displays, so proficiency in the second supports success in the first; parent-standard wording (understanding of many-to-one correspondence in displaying/reading graphs vs constructing and interpreting) corroborates this. Shared ancestry, code prefix and page proximity are treated as nomination signals only, not as the basis for direction. judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Content Standards (same grain, same rank 0) under Sub-strand 3 'Measurement- (Perimeter and Area)' of Strand 3 Geometry and Measurement, so shared hierarchy alone is not decisive. The bounded source excerpts show a substantive attribute progression within the same sub-strand: B4.3.3.1 develops perimeter of regular and irregular shapes via linear referents ('Estimate perimeter using referents for centimetre or metre', summing side lengths of irregular shapes, constructing rectangles for a given perimeter), while B4.3.3.2 extends the same measure-and-estimate-with-referents reasoning to a two-dimensional attribute ('Recognise that area is measured in square units', 'Estimate area by using referents for cm2 or m2'). judgment.rationale: Both are BASIC 4 Indicators (same rank 0) under Content Standard B4.2.2.2 'Solve one-step equations involving a symbol to represent an unknown number' in Sub-strand 2: Unknowns, Expressions and Equations. B4.2.2.2.4 is a bare solving technique for a given one-step equation ('guess and check'); B4.2.2.2.6 (LCs: 'represent a given addition or subtraction problem ... using a symbol to represent the unknown' and 'solve a given addition or subtraction problem ...') combines that solving skill with modelling a part-part-whole or comparison word problem with a symbol for the unknown. The substantive same-rank change is the addition of representation and contextual application onto the already-required solving step, so proficiency in solving a given one-step equation supports success in representing and solving the contextual problem, not the reverse. Judgment stays within the Indicator grain; shared parent, code prefix and page proximity alone were not treated as sufficient. Endpoint source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each), but the supplied statement texts and LCs are sufficient for this direction.

B4.1.1.1 establishes quantity and place-value understanding for multi-digit whole numerals to 100,000, i.e. foundational number sense and magnitude/position on the number sequence; B4.1.1.4 extends number meaning beyond whole numbers to interpreting negative and positive values in real-life contexts (per the source context label, describing situations using positive and negative values). Secure understanding of quantity and magnitude for whole numbers substantively supports success in interpreting signed numbers in context, giving a same-rank developmental direction from the second to the first SFI rather than mere shared-parent or code-prefix proximity (token/trigram overlap is weak and not the basis here).
